object: r5 round-2 theta kernel membership and alternatives
question: Is alpha2 in the column-parity kernel, and do alternatives keep beta2 and reach alpha3?
number: alpha2 NOT in kernel (exactly 20 nonzero parity columns in all 16 pairs); 59 active rows -> beta2 = 10 active rows (14 bits). Single-bit flips of alpha2 give beta2 rows 17-21 (> 10) and 0 of 1600 reach alpha3; same-column pairs (3200) give 9-12 rows and 0 of 3200 reach alpha3.
notes: Universe cell sha3-r5|round2.theta|theta|Q4. Method: own Keccak (tools/traillab/sha3_atlas/kk.py) on the 16 collision pairs of the pkgR5L certificates (all 16 reproduce the equal 4-lane digest, beta2 = trail BETA2 and alpha3 = trail alpha3 in the CP kernel, validated first); alternatives tested on the first 3 pairs: every single-bit flip of the round input (non-kernel) and every same-column bit pair (kernel-preserving), counting active chi rows of L(.) and reachability of the required next difference. Window only (16 pairs, local flips), not all kernel alternatives. alpha2 is fixed by the trail (all 16 pairs identical beta2). Local-flip test only; the exact alpha3' cluster (chi, 2^24) is the existing ex.py result and was not redone.
